correctness.rationale: Exact logarithmic period-2 equations verified both directions; the threshold equation is strictly monotone and has one solution with 0<c*<1-2/L; scalar fixed amplitude uniquely exists and f'(q)<-1 precisely below c*. For f=A/c, f'(0)>1 implies f(f(v))-v>0 near zero, while derivative f'(q)^2-1>0 implies it is negative just left of q. If iterates pass outside the positive zone, first f(v)=z yields the same negative endpoint before composition ceases, so IVT gives a genuine unequal pair. Reversing unequal amplitudes gives a distinct second orbit. All amplitudes lie strictly in (0,L), so map states are positive. High-precision 65-digit samples for (L,c)=(3,.15),(4,.2) reconstruct 3 orbits. Analytic proof, not those samples, handles universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The mathematical content is an all-L rigorous guarantee of three distinct antiphase primitive two-cycles under a nontrivial implicit coupling curve, not general antiphase existence or a numerical multistability report. Goldar et al. 2026 Theorem 6 supplies general fixed-point equations and numerical examples but no three-cycle multiplicity. Kulakov et al. 2022 present symmetric phase multistability and qualitative transitions via numerical nullcline solutions, not this exact implicit critical curve or global sufficient interval. In-slot prior antiphase theorem proves at least one and cannot imply three. Focused published-record searches revealed related models but no covering claim; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a genuine multiplicity question in a phase-multistable ecological map: a continuous, two-parameter rigorously delimited region contains at least three distinct antiphase primitive two-cycles even though one-cycle existence criteria do not determine the count. The threshold is an explicit monotone implicit curve and the extra cycles are constructed for all c below it, not inferred from isolated numerical examples. This provides a rigorous parameter-space benchmark for subsequent stability and basin studies; no claim of an exact census is made.
